pe.d.f: Frequency $f$ of the light; wavelength $\lambda = c/f$. Ultraviolet above $7.9\times10^{14}$ Hz (below 380 nm) is drawn grey
pe.d.V: Voltage $V$ of the collector relative to the emitter. Negative is a retarding voltage (turns electrons back)
pe.d.metal: Emitter metal and its work function $\Phi$
pe.d.power: Power $P$ of the light on the emitter: changes the photon rate and the current, not the electron energy
pe.d.classical: Overlay the prediction of classical wave theory (grey dashed) on both plots
pe.goal.photon: See that light is absorbed as photons of energy $hf$: there is a cutoff frequency, and the maximum kinetic energy $K_\text{max}$ does not depend on intensity
pe.goal.h: Measure stopping voltages for several frequencies and metals and find the slope $h/e$ and intercept $-\Phi/e$ of the $V_\text{stop}$–$f$ line
pe.obs.threshold: Lower the frequency until $hf < \Phi$: no electrons leave, however many photons arrive (Na: cutoff frequency $f_0 = \Phi/h$ = $5.51\times10^{14}$ Hz, $\lambda_0$ = 544 nm). The energy bar drops below the $\Phi$ line; the tick $f_0$ on the $V_\text{stop}$–$f$ plot marks the current metal
pe.obs.stop: Raise the retarding voltage: the current falls and reaches 0 at $V = -V_\text{stop}$; with a forward voltage it saturates
pe.obs.power: Change the light power: only the saturation current changes, in proportion; the stopping voltage stays
pe.obs.measure: The Measure button (tap or click) adds the current $(f, V_\text{stop})$ point. Each metal gives a parallel line, all with slope $h/e$
pe.obs.classical: Classical prediction: the stopping voltage grows with intensity and does not depend on frequency (horizontal dashed line), no cutoff frequency, and a delay $t_\text{cl}$ (Σ panel) of tens of minutes before emission. Observation contradicts all three
pe.as.yield: Quantum yield 1: each photon with $hf > \Phi$ frees one electron, so the saturation current is $I_\text{sat} = eP/(hf)$. Real photocathodes have a much lower yield
pe.as.dist: Photoelectron kinetic energies are uniform from 0 to $K_\text{max}$ and all directed at the collector (one dimension), so the current falls linearly with retarding voltage. Real curves are rounded by emission angles and the band structure, but $V_\text{stop}$ is set by $K_\text{max}$ alone
pe.as.phi: Work functions: typical values for polycrystalline surfaces; real values depend on the surface and crystal face
pe.as.ideal: Contact potential between the electrodes, space charge and reverse photocurrent from the collector are neglected
pe.as.data: Measured points are exact model values (no noise), so the fitted slope and intercept equal $h/e$ and $-\Phi/e$. The lines are a least-squares fit with one slope shared by all metals, drawn for metals with at least two points. At most 16 points (oldest dropped first), kept in the link
pe.as.classical: The classical prediction is the textbook wave picture: electron energy grows with intensity and exposure time and does not depend on frequency, with no cutoff. Its stopping-voltage scale (2 V per µW) is arbitrary; only the shape matters. Delay $t_\text{cl}$: time to collect energy $\Phi$ through a disc of radius 0.1 nm from light spread evenly over 1 cm². Measured delays are below $3\times10^{-9}$ s (Lawrence and Beams, 1928)
pe.as.uv: Above $15\times10^{14}$ Hz (below 200 nm) is vacuum ultraviolet, absorbed by air; the path from the source to the emitter is assumed evacuated
pe.as.display: Photon numbers and electron speeds on screen are display scales (photon rate ∝ $P/(hf)$, speed ∝ $\sqrt{K}$); the ammeter reads the model formula
